name: muse-codex-gpt-permanent-agent-registry
purpose: Permanent source-backed registry manifest for GPT chat and Codex code entities. This file registers every MUSE/AOS agent by canonical registry reference rather than duplicating brittle prompt text.

top_level_agents.description: Canonical/alias/mentioned registry for every distinct top-level agent name recovered across the MUSE/Hermes/AOS surfaces.

sub_agents.description: Division specialists, worker templates, Python runtime workers, R-personas, and product roles.

gpt_chat.responsibility: Muse brain: intake, strategy, critique, planning, evidence synthesis, owner handoff, mode-aware conversation.
gpt_chat.registry_rule: Before naming or dispatching an agent, consult the source_of_truth registry paths. Do not invent unregistered agents.

codex_code.responsibility: Codex lane: implementation review, bounded fixes, refactors, code audits, test/debug work, PR handoff packets.
codex_code.registry_rule: Before code-bearing work, route through the registered builder/reviewer lanes and preserve builder != reviewer for RC2+ work.

hard_rules: The registry is source-backed. The markdown registry files are canonical; this manifest is an index.
Never dispatch an unregistered agent name without adding it to the registry first.
Use the smallest capable layer: direct answer, AOS Council, specialist, skill, worker, or memory.
For code work, Codex/GPT must preserve the MUSE gates: Planning, Build, Review, Test, Security, Release, Owner Approval, Rollback.
Owner-gated actions remain owner-gated; this registry does not grant deploy, publish, credential, spending, or main-merge authority.
